Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 15:18:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: air-gapped / on-prem deployment viability & procurement questions

Thanks again for taking the call today, Sophie — really helpful to understand the NeuroBio constraints. Quick written recap and the asks I promised.

Summary of what we heard (from your team):
- Preferred deployment: Private (air-gapped) on-prem in your sealed lab environment. No external egress by default.
- Capacity target: steady-state inference for a single rack (8x A100-class GPUs or equivalent).
- Maintenance cadence: quarterly planned maintenance windows; emergency patches as needed with onsite approval.
- Security must-haves: support for customer-managed KMS / HSM, audit logs, and on-device key isolation.

Open questions we need from you to finalize a Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
1) Exact hardware you're planning to provision (chassis + GPU model + NIC topology). If you don't have exact SKUs yet, a target spec is fine.
2) Network topology / ability to provide a dedicated management VLAN for Redwood appliance comms during install (even if isolated afterwards).
3) Typical onsite change window length and blackout periods for patching.
4) Procurement lead contact for paperwork and shipping (we briefly mentioned Ari on the call).

Proposed next steps (low-friction):
- You: share the lab rack spec + Ari's procurement contact.
- Us: we will populate the Private Deploy Template (attached) with hardware compatibility notes and a draft on-prem MOP.
- Schedule: sync for a 30-min follow-up on Tue/Thu next week to walk the MAP draft.

Attached: Redwood_private_deploy_template.xlsx (skeleton we use for compatibility + MOP inputs).

If anything above looks off, flag and I'll correct. Otherwise I'll wait for the rack spec and Ari's contact and circulate a draft MAP.

Best,
Ben

Thanks Ben — appreciate the crisp recap. A few answers and clarifications below (quoting your Qs):

> 1) Exact hardware you're planning to provision (chassis + GPU model + NIC topology).
We haven't finalized SKU procurement yet; procurement is targeting an 8-GPU rack with the following baseline: 8x NVIDIA H100 SXM (or equivalent), dual 100GbE NICs (RDMA not required initially), redundant PSUs. We'll confirm SKUs by EOD next Friday (12 May).

> 2) Network topology / ability to provide a dedicated management VLAN for Redwood appliance comms during install.
We can carve a dedicated management VLAN that stays isolated from lab instruments. Outbound connectivity: currently restricted, but for install we can enable a temporary outbound tunnel to a staging host controlled by NeuroBio for installer ops. Post-install, egress will be disabled by default.

> 3) Typical onsite change window length and blackout periods for patching.
We run quarterly maintenance windows (2–4 hours typical) with a two-week notice. There are periodic blackout periods during major experiments (these are notified ~6 weeks in advance). Emergency patches require PI-level approval; average SLA to approve is 8 business hours.

> 4) Procurement lead contact for paperwork and shipping (we briefly mentioned Ari on the call).
Ari Park is our procurement manager: ari.park@neurobio.ai, +1 (206) 555-0122. Please loop Ari on any shipping paperwork and HAZMAT forms.

Attachments: lab-network-drawing.png (simplified rack/network diagram)

Additional asks from our end:
- Does Redwood support an offline upgrade MOP (mechanical swap + local package install) vs. remote patching? We need to understand the onsite maintenance steps (we won't allow a machine to phone home during most of the year).
- Can you outline the fallbacks if a patch fails offline (e.g., roll back steps, spares, and SLA expectations)?

Happy to hop on another quick call after you push the MAP draft.

— Sophie
Sophie Lamson | CTO, NeuroBio, Inc
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Recap: air-gapped / on-prem deployment viability & procurement questions

Sophie — great detail, thanks. Quick answers to the two operational asks and a proposed MAP outline.

Offline upgrade / MOP: yes — Redwood supports a fully offline maintenance path. We provide a documented Mechanical and Operational Procedure (MOP) that covers:
- Pre-staging: on-site precheck checklist (power, torque, firmware baselines).
- Package transfer: encrypted USB image transfer process signed by customer KMS/HSM attestation.
- Local install: step-by-step service user commands and validation checks.
- Verification: post-install health checks and tokenized audit log upload when allowed.

Fallbacks and rollback:
- We recommend an A/B partition strategy on the appliance image; if a patch fails, the device can boot the previous partition.
- Onsite spare: recommend one hot-swap node (same SKU) per rack for critical systems — our acceptance tests and runbook cover failover.
- If rollback not possible onsite, we provide a staged recovery plan and 24/7 escalation with dedicated engineer support for customers on Reserved/Dedicated plans.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) Confirm hardware SKUs & procurement contact (you / Ari) — due 2027-05-12
2) Redwood sends draft Private Deploy MAP + MOP template — due 2027-05-06 (attached: NeuroBio-MAP-DRAFT.docx)
3) Joint review call (30 min) to walk MAP — propose 2027-05-11 or 2027-05-13
4) On-site scope visit / validation (if agreed) — schedule after MAP sign-off

Fallback option: if procurement timelines slip, we can stand up a dedicated Reserved capacity pool in our US region to run the workload temporarily while hardware arrives; this requires a short security review but avoids downtime.

I'll attach the MAP draft and the Private template. If Ari can confirm SKUs by 12 May we'll be able to lock the install window and engineer allocation.

Attached: NeuroBio-MAP-DRAFT.docx

Best,
Ben
